blocks.text: IMPORTANT: These Terms form a binding agreement. They contain warranty disclaimers, limits of liability, customer compliance duties, suspension rights, and a dispute-resolution provision. Phone numbers are licensed for use and are not sold as property.

Please read these Terms of Service (the “Terms”) carefully. By creating an account, signing an Order Form, clicking to accept, paying an invoice, or accessing or using the Services, the individual accepting these Terms confirms that they have authority to bind the Customer and agrees that Customer will comply with these Terms. If Customer does not agree, Customer must not access or use the Services.
1. Definitions

“Affiliate” means an entity that controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with a party. “Authorized User” means an employee, contractor, agent, or other person Customer permits to use the Services. “Customer,” “you,” or “your” means the person or entity ordering or using the Services. “Customer Data” means information, content, prompts, recordings, transcripts, contact data, business rules, credentials, and other materials submitted to or processed through the Services on Customer’s behalf.

“Digital Employee” means an AI-enabled software agent configured to perform approved tasks, which may include answering or placing calls, responding to messages, routing communications, scheduling appointments, collecting information, and interacting with approved systems. “Order Form” means an ordering document, online checkout, statement of work, proposal, or similar transaction record identifying Services, fees, usage allowances, and any special terms. “Services” means Orbit’s website, software, Digital Employees, phone numbers, voice or messaging functionality, integrations, professional services, support, and related offerings.
2. Eligibility, Accounts, and Business Use

Customer must be legally capable of entering into a contract and, if accepting for an entity, authorized to bind that entity. Unless an Order Form expressly states otherwise, the Services are offered for legitimate business use and not for personal, family, or household use. Customer must provide accurate, complete, and current account, billing, tax, ownership, and contact information.

Customer is responsible for all activity under its accounts and credentials, for maintaining appropriate administrative controls and strong authentication, and for promptly notifying Orbit at admin@orbitsystems.ai of suspected unauthorized access. Customer may not share accounts except with Authorized Users and may not allow access by a competitor for benchmarking or reverse engineering.
3. Orders; Service Configuration

Each Order Form is incorporated into these Terms. If documents conflict, the following order applies unless an Order Form expressly states otherwise: (a) a signed data processing addendum for privacy matters; (b) the Order Form; (c) these Terms; and (d) documentation or policies referenced here. A purchase order is for administrative convenience only and does not modify this agreement.

Customer is responsible for reviewing and approving its Digital Employee’s identity, greeting, disclosures, knowledge sources, scripts, workflows, escalation paths, allowed actions, integrations, call-routing rules, and test results before production use. Customer must keep that configuration accurate and must use human review and fallback procedures appropriate to the risk of each use case.
4. Digital Employees and AI Limitations

Digital Employees use probabilistic technology and may produce inaccurate, incomplete, delayed, unexpected, or offensive output; misunderstand speakers; fail to complete a task; or take an unintended action within configured permissions. Customer must independently evaluate outputs and must not treat a Digital Employee as a human or licensed professional.

Unless Orbit expressly agrees in a signed Order Form, Customer will not use the Services to make final decisions concerning employment, housing, lending, insurance, healthcare diagnosis or treatment, legal rights, education admissions, government benefits, public safety, or another high-impact or regulated determination. Customer must provide meaningful human oversight where required by law or reasonably necessary to prevent harm.

Customer must ensure that callers and message recipients receive any disclosures required by law, which may include disclosure that they are interacting with an automated or AI system and that a communication may be recorded or monitored. Customer may not falsely present a Digital Employee as a particular real person or use a voice, likeness, identity, or other personal attribute without all required rights and permissions.
5. Telephony, Phone Numbers, Messaging, and Emergency Services
5.1 Limited right to use numbers

Orbit or its communications providers may provision, host, port, or assign telephone numbers for Customer’s use with the Services. A number is not sold to Customer and Customer acquires no ownership, property, or perpetual right in it. Customer receives only a limited, revocable right to use an assigned number during the applicable Subscription Term, subject to law, numbering rules, carrier requirements, availability, and these Terms.
5.2 Provisioning, reassignment, and continuity

Number availability is not guaranteed. Regulators, carriers, upstream providers, or Orbit may reclaim, replace, suspend, or reassign numbers where required by law, to address fraud or abuse, after nonpayment or termination, or for technical or operational reasons. Orbit will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide notice when practicable but does not guarantee continuous availability, geographic identity, caller-name display, reputation, deliverability, or compatibility with every carrier or destination.
5.3 Porting

Port-in and port-out requests require complete and accurate documentation, account standing, cooperation, and compliance with carrier procedures. Customer authorizes Orbit and its providers to submit and process porting documentation on Customer’s behalf. Customer remains responsible for fees and usage until a port is completed. Orbit does not guarantee that a number can be ported or retained. Orbit will not unreasonably prevent a lawful port-out requested before termination, but may require payment of undisputed past-due amounts and completion of required verification, except where law prohibits those conditions.
5.4 Customer’s communications responsibility

Customer is the initiator, sender, and party responsible for communications made or received through its account, even when a Digital Employee generates, selects, routes, or delivers content. Customer must maintain and be able to produce legally sufficient evidence of consent, opt-in, opt-out, suppression, and campaign records. Customer must honor revocation and do-not-call requests promptly and maintain appropriate internal suppression lists.
5.5 Registration and carrier programs

Customer must complete all required identity, know-your-customer, caller-ID, branded calling, toll-free verification, A2P or campaign registration, and similar carrier or industry processes. Customer may not provide false registration information, rotate numbers to avoid enforcement, alter caller ID deceptively, or use numbers that Customer is not authorized to use. Registration or approval does not establish legal compliance or guarantee call completion or message delivery.
5.6 Emergency services

THE SERVICES ARE NOT A REPLACEMENT FOR 911, E911, 988, EMERGENCY DISPATCH, ALARM MONITORING, OR ANY OTHER EMERGENCY SERVICE UNLESS AN ORDER FORM EXPRESSLY IDENTIFIES A SPECIFIC EMERGENCY-CALLING FEATURE AND ITS TERMS. CUSTOMER MUST NOT ROUTE OR RELY ON EMERGENCY COMMUNICATIONS THROUGH THE SERVICES OTHERWISE. CUSTOMER MUST INFORM AUTHORIZED USERS OF THIS LIMITATION AND MAINTAIN AN INDEPENDENT, RELIABLE MEANS TO CONTACT EMERGENCY SERVICES.

If an Order Form expressly includes emergency calling, Customer must provide and maintain accurate registered-location information and comply with all testing, labeling, notification, and use instructions. Emergency calling may have limitations described in the applicable Order Form or provider terms, including limitations during internet, power, device, configuration, or service outages. Nothing in these Terms waives a nonwaivable legal obligation.
6. Acceptable Use and Communications Compliance

Customer will comply with all laws, regulations, codes, carrier rules, and industry requirements applicable to Customer, its content, and its communications, including as applicable the Telephone Consumer Protection Act, Telemarketing Sales Rule, state mini-TCPA and recording laws, National Do Not Call rules, caller-ID and anti-spoofing requirements, CAN-SPAM, privacy and biometric laws, and messaging program requirements.
Customer must not use or permit use of the Services to:

make calls or send messages without legally sufficient consent, required identification, or a working opt-out mechanism; contact a person after consent is revoked or contrary to an applicable do-not-call or suppression list;

send spam, unlawful marketing, scams, phishing, deceptive solicitations, fraudulent offers, or content that misrepresents the caller, sender, purpose, price, material terms, or relationship with Orbit or another party;

engage in unlawful debt collection, harassment, threats, hate, exploitation, trafficking, illegal gambling, controlled-substance transactions, weapons trafficking, or the promotion or facilitation of illegal goods or services;

impersonate a person or organization; spoof or manipulate caller identification; mislead a recipient about the use of AI; or use a voice, recording, likeness, trademark, or other protected material without authorization;

generate or distribute malware; probe, scan, disrupt, overload, or bypass security or usage controls; scrape or exfiltrate data without authorization; or interfere with networks, carriers, recipients, or other customers;

use the Services for emergency dispatch, safety-critical control, or a high-impact decision except under a signed Order Form expressly permitting the use case and allocating compliance responsibilities;
resell, sublicense, transfer, or provide access to a phone number or Service except as expressly permitted in an Order Form; or

Orbit may investigate suspected violations and may block traffic, disable features or numbers, preserve evidence, or cooperate with carriers, platforms, regulators, or law enforcement where reasonably necessary. Customer must provide information reasonably requested to verify consent, identity, campaign purpose, data sources, or compliance.
7. Customer Data; Privacy; Call Recording

As between the parties, Customer retains its rights in Customer Data. Customer grants Orbit and its subprocessors a nonexclusive, worldwide right to host, copy, transmit, modify, create technical derivatives from, and otherwise process Customer Data only as reasonably necessary to provide, secure, support, improve, and comply with law regarding the Services, subject to any applicable data processing addendum and privacy policy.

Customer represents and warrants that it has provided all notices and obtained all rights, permissions, consents, and lawful bases necessary for Orbit and its providers to process Customer Data as contemplated. Customer is solely responsible for deciding whether, when, and how calls or messages are recorded, transcribed, analyzed, or retained, and for giving all required one-party, all-party, employee, consumer, biometric, and AI notices and obtaining all required consents.

Customer will not submit payment-card data, government identification numbers, authentication secrets, protected health information, or other highly sensitive data unless an Order Form expressly authorizes that data type and identifies applicable safeguards. Customer must configure collection and retention to minimize data and limit access. Orbit may delete Customer Data after termination in accordance with its retention practices, legal obligations, and any Order Form.
7.1 Children’s Privacy

The Services are intended for business use and are not directed to children under 13. Customer must not configure or use the Services to solicit or knowingly collect personal information from children under 13 unless Orbit has expressly approved the use case in a written Order Form and the parties have implemented all legally required notices, verifiable parental-consent procedures, security measures, retention limits, and parental rights. Customer must promptly notify Orbit at legal@orbitsystems.ai if Customer believes a child’s personal information was collected improperly.

Third-party services are governed by their own terms and privacy practices. 9. Fees, Billing, Taxes, and Payment

Customer will pay the subscription, setup, usage, number, carrier, messaging, professional-service, and other fees stated in the Order Form. Unless stated otherwise, recurring fees are billed in advance and metered or pass-through usage is billed in arrears. Fees are stated in U.S. dollars, non-cancelable during the committed Subscription Term, and nonrefundable except as expressly provided in these Terms or an Order Form.

Each invoice will itemize, as applicable, recurring subscription charges, setup or professional-service fees, telephone-number charges, metered voice usage, messaging usage, other usage-based charges, carrier or provider pass-through charges, regulatory assessments, surcharges, credits, and taxes. Customer authorizes Orbit and its payment processor, including Stripe, to charge Customer’s payment method for all amounts due, including recurring subscription fees, metered usage, taxes, and approved overages. Invoices are due on receipt unless the Order Form states another period. Customer must dispute an invoice in writing within 30 days after its date and provide reasonable detail; otherwise, the invoice is deemed accepted to the extent permitted by law. Customer may not initiate a chargeback for a good-faith contractual dispute without first contacting Orbit at finance@orbitsystems.ai and allowing at least 10 business days to investigate, but this does not waive any nonwaivable cardholder right.

Fees exclude sales, use, excise, telecommunications, communications-services, 911 or E911, universal-service, regulatory-recovery, value-added, withholding, and similar taxes, fees, or assessments. A trial or pilot is governed by these Terms and any stated limits and may be changed or ended at any time unless an Order Form says otherwise. The initial subscription term begins on the date stated in the Order Form or, if none, when paid access begins. Unless the Order Form says otherwise, subscriptions renew automatically for successive periods equal to the initial term until either party gives written nonrenewal notice at least 30 days before the current term ends.

Orbit may change fees for a renewal term by providing at least 30 days’ notice. Any consumer cancellation right required by applicable law remains unaffected, although the Services are intended for business use.
11. Suspension and Termination

Orbit may suspend some or all Services immediately if: (a) fees are overdue; (b) Customer’s use presents a security, legal, fraud, safety, carrier, payment-network, or operational risk; (c) a regulator, carrier, upstream provider, court, or law-enforcement authority requests or requires action; (d) Customer violates Sections 5, 6, or 7; or (e) suspension is reasonably necessary to prevent material harm. Either party may terminate an Order Form for an uncured material breach after 30 days’ written notice, except a breach incapable of cure may permit immediate termination. Orbit may terminate immediately for unlawful or fraudulent use, repeated policy violations, insolvency, or loss of a necessary carrier or provider relationship. Upon termination, Customer must stop using the Services and numbers, pay all accrued amounts, and export Customer Data before the applicable access or retention period ends. Orbit and its licensors own the Services, software, models, workflows, documentation, templates, improvements, and all related intellectual property, excluding Customer Data. Subject to payment and compliance, Orbit grants Customer a limited, nonexclusive, nontransferable, nonsublicensable right during the Subscription Term to access and use the Services for Customer’s internal business purposes and authorized customer interactions.

If Customer provides feedback, Customer grants Orbit a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free right to use it without restriction or attribution. Orbit will use Customer’s name or logo in public marketing only with Customer’s prior written consent. Orbit may identify Customer privately to service providers as necessary to deliver the Services.
13. Confidentiality

Each party may receive nonpublic information designated as confidential or that reasonably should be understood as confidential. The receiving party will use it only to perform or exercise rights under the agreement, protect it using at least reasonable care, and disclose it only to personnel and providers who need to know and are bound by confidentiality duties. These duties do not apply to information lawfully known without restriction, independently developed, rightfully received from another source, or public through no breach. EXCEPT FOR THE EXPRESS WARRANTY ABOVE AND TO THE MAXIMUM EXTENT PERMITTED BY LAW, THE SERVICES ARE PROVIDED “AS IS” AND “AS AVAILABLE.” ORBIT DISCLAIMS ALL IMPLIED OR STATUTORY WARRANTIES, INCLUDING MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE, TITLE, NON-INFRINGEMENT, ACCURACY, QUIET ENJOYMENT, AND WARRANTIES ARISING FROM COURSE OF DEALING OR USAGE OF TRADE. 15. Indemnification

Customer will defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Orbit, its Affiliates, providers, and their personnel from third-party claims, investigations, fines, penalties, damages, losses, costs, and reasonable attorneys’ fees arising from or relating to: (a) Customer Data, scripts, campaigns, products, or instructions; (b) Customer’s or an Authorized User’s use of the Services; (c) calls, recordings, texts, email, or other communications initiated, received, or processed for Customer; (d) Customer’s violation of law, consent or disclosure obligations, carrier rules, or these Terms; or (e) infringement, misappropriation, fraud, impersonation, or harmful conduct attributable to Customer.

The indemnified party must promptly notify the indemnifying party, allow it to control the defense and settlement, and provide reasonable cooperation. A settlement may not admit fault by or impose a nonmonetary obligation on the indemnified party without written consent.

TO THE MAXIMUM EXTENT PERMITTED BY LAW, NEITHER PARTY WILL BE LIABLE FOR INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, EXEMPLARY, PUNITIVE, OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES, OR FOR LOST PROFITS, REVENUE, GOODWILL, BUSINESS OPPORTUNITIES, OR DATA, EVEN IF ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY. Multiple claims do not enlarge the cap. The parties agree that these limitations allocate risk and are a material basis of the bargain.

These Terms and each Order Form are governed by the laws of the State of Florida, without regard to conflict-of-laws rules. blocks.text: This Privacy Policy explains how Orbit Systems Ai, LLC ("Orbit," "we," "us," or "our") collects, uses, discloses, and protects personal information when you visit our websites, communicate with us, purchase or use our services, or interact with an AI-powered digital employee operated by or through Orbit (collectively, the "Services").

This Policy does not replace a customer’s own privacy notice. When Orbit processes calls, messages, recordings, transcripts, contact data, or other content for a business customer, that customer generally determines why and how the information is processed, and Orbit acts as its service provider or processor. Direct privacy requests about those interactions should normally be sent to the business you contacted.
1. Scope and Our Role

This Policy applies to visitors, prospective and current customers, authorized users, vendors, business contacts, callers, message senders, and other people whose information is processed through the Services.
Depending on the context, Orbit may act as:
a controller or business for information used to administer our websites, accounts, billing, sales, security, and direct customer relationships; or
a processor or service provider for Customer Content processed on a customer’s documented instructions, subject to the applicable services agreement, order form, or data processing addendum.

If a customer configures a Digital Employee for a regulated or sensitive workflow, the customer is responsible for determining whether the use is lawful, providing required notices, obtaining required permissions, and configuring appropriate retention, access, and escalation rules.
2. Information We Collect
Information you provide
Contact and business information, such as name, email address, telephone number, job title, company name, billing address, and support details.

Account and transaction information, such as plan, subscription, invoice, payment status, and limited payment-related details. Payment card information is generally collected and processed by Stripe, not stored directly by Orbit.
Customer configuration and content, such as business knowledge, scripts, greetings, calendars, routing rules, escalation contacts, appointment information, integrations, prompts, and files.
Communications, including emails, support requests, meeting notes, survey responses, and other information you choose to provide.
Telephony, messaging, and AI interaction data
Phone numbers, caller and recipient numbers, message addresses, timestamps, call duration, routing data, carrier data, delivery status, and similar communications metadata.
Audio recordings, voicemail, call or message content, transcripts, summaries, sentiment or intent labels, extracted fields, and AI-generated responses, when the feature is enabled.
Contact details or appointment information provided during an interaction, such as name, email, reason for calling, preferred time, and confirmation status.
Quality, safety, and operational signals, such as interruptions, transfers, failed tool calls, abuse indicators, and human-review outcomes.
Website, device, and automatically collected data
IP address, browser and device type, operating system, pages viewed, referring URL, approximate location derived from IP, timestamps, identifiers, and diagnostic logs.
Cookies and similar technologies used for essential operation, preferences, security, performance, and—where permitted—analytics or marketing.
Information from other sources

We may receive information from our customers, authorized users, integration partners, telecommunications carriers, number providers, payment processors, identity or fraud-prevention providers, public sources, and vendors that support the Services.
3. Phone Numbers and Telecommunications Services

Orbit may obtain, provision, assign, port, host, or administer telephone numbers and related communications capabilities for customers. A phone number is a communications resource governed by carrier, numbering, portability, emergency-service, anti-fraud, and regulatory requirements; it is not sold as personal property. Availability and continued use may depend on the applicable order, carrier rules, lawful-use requirements, account status, and regulatory eligibility.

To provision or manage a number, we and our providers may process customer identity and business information, service address, authorized representative details, emergency-service information, porting records, letters of authorization, tax or registration details, call and message metadata, and compliance documentation. We may disclose this information to carriers, numbering administrators, verification providers, emergency-service vendors, or authorities when reasonably necessary to activate, transfer, secure, or lawfully operate the service.
4. Call Recording, Transcription, and AI Disclosure

Depending on the customer’s configuration, telephone or online voice interactions may be recorded, transcribed, summarized, analyzed, or reviewed by automated systems or authorized personnel. An AI voice or Digital Employee may participate in the interaction.

Recording and consent laws vary by jurisdiction. Orbit’s customer is responsible for choosing a lawful configuration and for providing notices and obtaining consent when required. Orbit may provide technical controls or sample disclosures, but those tools do not constitute legal advice or guarantee compliance. Where Orbit controls the interaction directly, we use notices or consent mechanisms appropriate to the circumstances and applicable law.

If you do not wish to be recorded or interact with an automated system, follow the instructions presented during the interaction, request a human or alternate channel where available, or end the call. A requested alternative may not be available for every service.
5. How We Use Information
We use personal information to:
provide, configure, maintain, route, and improve the Services, including Digital Employees, phone numbers, calls, messages, appointments, integrations, and customer dashboards;
authenticate users, administer accounts, provide support, communicate about service events, and fulfill customer instructions;
process subscriptions, invoices, payments, refunds, taxes, and related financial records;
monitor availability, diagnose failures, prevent spam, fraud, abuse, unlawful communications, and security incidents, and enforce our agreements;
evaluate quality and performance, develop features, and conduct research using aggregated or de-identified data where feasible;
comply with law, carrier and numbering obligations, valid legal process, and regulatory requests; and
send product or marketing communications where permitted, subject to applicable choices and consent requirements.

Orbit does not use Customer Content to train a generalized AI model for unrelated customers unless the customer agreement expressly permits it or the customer provides authorization. We may use de-identified or aggregated information that cannot reasonably identify an individual to operate, secure, analyze, and improve the Services.
6. Legal Bases for Processing

Where a legal basis is required, we process personal information as necessary to perform a contract, comply with legal obligations, protect vital interests, pursue legitimate interests that are not overridden by applicable rights (such as operating, securing, and improving the Services), or with consent. A customer may rely on different legal bases for Customer Content and is responsible for documenting them.
7. How We Disclose Information
We may disclose personal information to:

service providers and subprocessors that support cloud hosting, AI and speech processing, telecommunications, phone-number provisioning, messaging, email, analytics, customer support, security, identity verification, and professional services;
Stripe and other financial partners for payment processing, fraud prevention, authentication, analytics, and related business services. Stripe processes information under its own privacy policy;
the customer on whose behalf a Digital Employee or communications workflow operates, including its authorized users and connected systems;
carriers, numbering administrators, emergency-service providers, communications registries, and compliance vendors;

government authorities, courts, regulators, law enforcement, or other parties where we believe disclosure is required or permitted by law, needed to protect rights or safety, or necessary to address fraud or abuse; and

a buyer, investor, lender, adviser, or successor in connection with an actual or proposed merger, financing, acquisition, reorganization, or sale of assets, subject to appropriate confidentiality protections.

We do not sell personal information for money. We also do not knowingly share personal information for cross-context behavioral advertising. If our practices change, we will provide legally required notices and choices.
8. Stripe and Payments

We use Stripe for payments and related business services. Stripe may collect personal data, including transaction data, contact and billing information, device identifiers, and information collected through cookies or similar technologies. Stripe uses this information to process transactions, authenticate users, prevent and detect fraud, provide analytics, and operate and improve its services. Stripe’s handling of personal information is governed by its own privacy policy at https://stripe.com/privacy.
9. Data Retention

We retain personal information for the period reasonably necessary for the purposes described in this Policy, including to provide the Services, follow customer instructions, maintain security, resolve disputes, enforce agreements, and satisfy legal, accounting, carrier, tax, and compliance obligations. Retention depends on the type of information, sensitivity, customer configuration, contractual commitments, legal requirements, and whether the information is needed for fraud prevention or service continuity.

Customer Content, including recordings and transcripts, is retained according to the customer’s configured settings or contract and may be deleted or de-identified after the applicable period. Deletion from active systems may not immediately remove information from encrypted backups, logs, legal holds, or records that must be retained by law. Customers should set retention periods appropriate to their use case and jurisdiction.
10. Security

We use administrative, technical, and physical safeguards designed to protect personal information, such as access controls, authentication, encryption in transit and where appropriate at rest, logging, vendor review, tenant separation, least-privilege access, and incident-response procedures. No system, transmission, or storage method is completely secure, and we cannot guarantee absolute security. Customers are responsible for securing their credentials, endpoints, integrations, and authorized-user access.
11. Cookies and Online Choices

You can control cookies through browser settings and, where offered, our consent tools. Blocking essential cookies may prevent parts of the Services from functioning. You may unsubscribe from marketing email using the link in the message; we may still send transactional or service communications. Depending on where you live and subject to exceptions, you may have the right to request access to or a copy of personal information; correction; deletion; restriction or objection; portability; withdrawal of consent; or an appeal of a denied request. These categories may include identifiers; customer records; commercial information; internet or electronic-network activity; geolocation approximated from IP; audio, electronic, and similar information; professional or employment-related information; and inferences derived from interactions.

The Services are intended for business use and are not directed to children under 13. If we learn that a child’s personal information was collected without legally sufficient authorization, we will take reasonable steps to delete or appropriately restrict that information and, where applicable, assist the relevant Customer. A parent or legal guardian may request access to, correction of, or deletion of a child’s information by contacting legal@orbitsystems.ai. Customers must maintain an independent means of emergency communication and follow all emergency-address registration and testing instructions supplied by Orbit or an underlying provider.

Orbit investigates reported failures involving approved knowledge, prompts, routing, integrations, appointment workflows, and escalation logic.
